repair facilities. One source statement: Calliope Graving Dock at Devonport, lengthened by 40 ft (work about six months, decided late 1942) to take Indianapolis-class heavy cruisers
the Calliope Graving Dock at Davenport ... was enlarged to take heavy cruisers of the Indianapolis class
column14: Decision "late in 1942", work "about six months"; completion date inferred as 1943. The text spells it Davenport; Carter (BBBO-6) prints Bevenport. Before the extension Auckland had meager drydock facilities for major and intermediate ships.

repair facilities. One source statement: In 1943 Auckland could overhaul four attack transports at once; most important NZ repair port, 282 vessels repaired in 11 months of 1943 (February excluded)
4 vessels of the attack-transport type could receive overhaul concurrently with smaller craft
column14: Work was farmed to 112 independent firms when it exceeded the dockyard. Describes 1943, not 1942.

repair facilities. One source statement: USS Rigel (AR-11), repair ship
arrived at Auckland to add her equipment and personnel to the repair and construction facilities offered by that port ... Between then and November
column14: Arrived 16 May; on 8 Nov embarked Army units, sailed 9 Nov for New Caledonia (same entry). Carter (BBBO-4) puts Rigel at Auckland in late July 1942 and proposed she stay there to add to dockyard repair capacity.

column14: No opening date for Buin/Kahili in Aug-Sep 1942; value left empty. Brief says Buin/Kahili not yet built in this period; consistent with this.

pair of G4M1 Bettys daily from 9 Jan 1943

The cruisers had practically no repair facilities other than ship's force and what the overworked Rigel had

it was never commensurate in size or capacity with some of the other activities there
